headline: A 2022 law lets ICE officers in the Shadow Wolves patrol unit, and similar units elsewhere, be reclassified as ICE special agents after completing required training.
what_it_does: The law allows U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to reclassify officers in the tactical patrol unit on Tohono O'odham Nation land, known as the Shadow Wolves, as ICE special agents once they finish certain required training. Officers in a comparable unit, no matter where they are stationed, may also be reclassified after completing that training. The Department of Homeland Security and the Government Accountability Office must each separately study and report on the best ways to expand the Shadow Wolves program.

who_it_affects.group: Officers in the Shadow Wolves tactical patrol unit on Tohono O'odham Nation land
who_it_affects.how: They may be reclassified as ICE special agents after completing the required training.

who_it_affects.group: Officers in comparable tactical units elsewhere
who_it_affects.how: They may also be reclassified as ICE special agents after completing the required training, regardless of their location.
The agency is given authority to make these reclassifications.

who_it_affects.group: Department of Homeland Security and Government Accountability Office
who_it_affects.how: Each must study and report on the best processes for expanding the Shadow Wolves program.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on April 19, 2022; the summary does not give a separate start date for the reclassification provisions.
